text:
Mattias Ekholm is 36 and still on the Oilers' top pair, playing 21 minutes a night for a team that has won four straight under Mike Babcock. His 10 points in 19 games look like a solid season for a defense-first defenseman, and his on-ice numbers look even better.

Too good, in one respect. Edmonton has scored almost 19 more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, the biggest on-ice luck number on our board, and his own three goals came on barely one expected. That is the Oilers' finishing (and Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl) doing a lot of lifting, and it will not last at this rate.

The underlying play is still good. Edmonton takes 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him out there, almost seven points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at the 98th percentile among defensemen last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net at the 98th percentile too, with 42% of his shots off the rush. When the bounces cool, that's the player who'll be left.
